info.name: ATW Backend — Worker Face Enrollment
info.description:
# ATW Backend — Worker Face Enrollment

Admin-triggered enrollment of a worker's face template for a future attendance face-match feature - a
dedicated `faceauth` module, not part of `kyc`. Whether a worker has a face template on file is an
independent fact, with its own `faceauth.*` permissions separate from `workers.*`/`kyc.*`. Nested under
`/admin/workers/{workerId}/face-enrollment` for API discoverability even though it's served by a
different module's controller (same precedent as Worker KYC).

**Run order:** every request here only needs an existing `{{workerId}}` - there is no create-order
dependency between the three requests themselves, and this collection never creates a worker. Get one
from the Worker collection (written concurrently alongside this one) and set it as an environment
variable first. A sensible manual run: **Get Face Enrollment** (see the not-enrolled placeholder) →
**Enroll / Re-enroll Worker Face** → **Get Face Enrollment** again (now enrolled) → **Remove Face
Enrollment** → **Get Face Enrollment** once more (back to the placeholder).

**Shared conventions across every request in this folder:**
- `GET` never 404s - a worker who hasn't enrolled gets a placeholder body (`enrolled: false`, every
  other field `null`) back, not an error. There is no separate "has this worker enrolled" endpoint;
  `data.enrolled` on the `GET` response is the only way to ask that through this API.
- `PUT` is both enroll *and* re-enroll - re-enrolling fully **overwrites** the previous template, with
  no history of past enrollments kept, only ever the current one.
- `DELETE` is a "make sure nothing is enrolled" operation, not "delete this specific enrollment" - it is
  **not** an error if the worker had nothing enrolled to begin with.
- Locally and in tests, `atw.face-auth.provider` is unset and defaults to a stub adapter that accepts
  any photo as good-quality and live. The 422 quality/liveness failure examples below can only actually
  be exercised against a real `atw.face-auth.provider=python` deployment of the separate face-auth
  service.
- The Worker module's own `GET /workers/{id}` already embeds this exact enrollment shape as its
  `faceEnrollment` field, and its list endpoint carries a lighter `faceEnrolledAt` timestamp - most
  front-end screens won't need **Get Face Enrollment** below at all except around the enroll/re-enroll/
  remove actions themselves.

For admin login/2FA, see **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json**; for staff/role administration,
see **ATW-RBAC-Staff.postman_collection.json**; for reference/lookup data, see
**ATW-Masterdata.postman_collection.json** (also this collection's style template).

Every endpoint is versioned under `/api/v1/` and returns the same envelope:

```
{ "success": boolean, "data": <payload> | null, "error": <ApiError> | null }
```

`ApiError` shape: `{"code": string, "message": string, "fieldErrors": [{"field","message"}] | null, "timestamp": ISO-8601 string, "traceId": string | null}`. `fieldErrors` is populated only for `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses that came from `@Valid` request-body validation; it's `null`/omitted for every other error, including other `VALIDATION_ERROR` responses raised programmatically (e.g. "Unknown permission code(s)"). `traceId` echoes the `X-Correlation-Id` request header when present — include it when reporting a bug.

## Running this collection

Select the **ATW Backend - Local** environment first, and run **Login** / **Verify OTP** from the
Auth & Account collection to populate `{{accessToken}}` — every request here requires it, plus the
matching `faceauth.*` permission. Then set `{{workerId}}` to a real worker id (create one via the
Worker collection, or paste in an existing one) - nothing below creates a worker itself.

1. **Get Face Enrollment** has no dependency on the other two - safe to run first against any
   `{{workerId}}`.
2. **Enroll / Re-enroll Worker Face** needs an actual image file attached to its `file` form-data part
   (Postman can't supply one for you - pick any small PNG/JPEG/WEBP under 2MB) and `consentGiven` left
   at `true`.
3. **Remove Face Enrollment** depends on nothing - it succeeds whether or not step 2 ran.

## Error codes that can appear on (almost) any endpoint

These are produced centrally — by `GlobalExceptionHandler`, by Spring Security's entry point / access-denied handler, or by the two security filters that run before a controller is even reached — so they are **not** re-documented on every individual request below; only an endpoint's *specific* codes and triggers are. Two pairs are easy to confuse and worth reading carefully:

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | A `@Valid` request-body field failed Bean Validation (`fieldErrors[]` present), or a service-level input check failed (no `fieldErrors`). |
| `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | 400 | Request body is missing or isn't valid JSON. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | `Content-Type` isn't `application/json`. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | **No bearer token was presented at all**, or it's malformed/expired/signature-invalid. Produced by Spring Security itself, before any controller runs. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | A **business-level** auth failure on an endpoint that doesn't require a token in the first place — bad login credentials, a locked/disabled account, an invalid refresh/reset/invite token. Same HTTP status as `UNAUTHENTICATED` above, different meaning: this means "the token/credential you supplied is bad", not "you supplied nothing". |
| `SESSION_REVOKED` | 401 | The bearer token parses fine, but the admin's `security_version` has moved on since it was issued (password changed/reset, or their role assignment changed), or the account is no longer `ACTIVE`. The client must discard tokens and log in again — refreshing won't help, the refresh token was revoked too. |
| `MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD` | 403 | Authenticated, but the token's `mustChangePassword` flag is set and this isn't `/admin/account/me` or `/admin/account/change-password`. |
| `ACCESS_DENIED` | 403 | Authenticated, but lacking the specific permission the endpoint requires. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests to one of the 6 public, abuse-prone auth endpoints from the same IP within the window — default 10 requests/60s, **per endpoint**, not pooled across them. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The **URL itself** doesn't match any endpoint (a routing miss — typo'd path, wrong version prefix, etc). |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The URL is valid, but the specific id in it (a staff id, role id, ...) doesn't exist. Different from `NOT_FOUND` above — don't conflate "no such route" with "no such record". |
| `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | 405 | Right URL, wrong HTTP verb. |
| `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` | 422 | Input is syntactically well-formed but violates a business rule (e.g. "system roles cannot be modified", a privilege-escalation attempt, self/super-admin protection). |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | Either an endpoint's own duplicate check (most common — a friendlier, specific message), or a generic last-resort safety net when a unique-constraint violation reaches the database despite an earlier application-level check passing (a genuine race between two concurrent requests) — that fallback case always carries the same generic message, regardless of which field collided. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Full detail (stack trace) is logged server-side against the same `traceId` returned to the client; never returned in the response body itself. |

**Specific to this module:** `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` above does **not** apply to any endpoint in this
collection. `GET` returns a not-enrolled placeholder instead of 404 for any `workerId` at all (real or
not - confirmed against `FaceAuthServiceImpl.getEnrollment`, which never checks the `worker` table).
Neither `PUT` nor `DELETE` checks worker existence either; a `PUT` against a `workerId` that doesn't
actually exist as a worker would instead fail with a generic `CONFLICT`/409 from the underlying
foreign-key constraint - an edge case a normal UI flow should never hit, since `workerId` always comes
from an already-loaded worker page.

## Documentation cross-references

- **ATW-Auth-Account.postman_collection.json** — login/2FA and a caller's own account self-service.
- **ATW-RBAC-Staff.postman_collection.json** — role/permission management and staff administration.
- **ATW-Masterdata.postman_collection.json** — departments/industries/designations/skills/minimum-wage
  reference data, and this collection's style template.
- `FRONTEND_HANDOVER.md` / `HANDOVER.md` — broader project handover context.
- The **Worker** and **Worker KYC** admin APIs (collections written concurrently alongside this one)
  own the `workerId` this whole module keys off of, and surface this module's data without a separate
  call via `WorkerResponse.faceEnrollment` / `WorkerSummaryResponse.faceEnrolledAt`.

item.name: Worker - Face Enrollment
item.description: Three endpoints covering the full lifecycle of one worker's face template: check status, enroll/re-enroll, and remove. All three are nested under `/admin/workers/{workerId}/face-enrollment` and gated by `faceauth.*` permissions (separate from `workers.*`/`kyc.*`). See this collection's top description for the full run order, shared conventions, and error-code table.

request.description:
**Permission:** `faceauth.view`.

Never returns 404, even for a `workerId` that doesn't exist or has simply never enrolled - a not-enrolled placeholder (`enrolled: false`, every other field `null`) comes back instead, so a caller never needs a separate existence check before rendering an enrollment panel. This read performs no check against the worker table itself either way (confirmed against `FaceAuthServiceImpl.getEnrollment`) - don't rely on it to validate that a `workerId` is real.

There is no separate "is this worker enrolled" endpoint - `data.enrolled` here is the only way to ask that through this API. `photoUrl` is a short-lived (about 15 minutes) signed Azure Blob URL; call this endpoint again for a fresh one rather than caching it past expiry.

response.name: 200 - Not enrolled (placeholder, not a 404)
response.body: {"success": true, "data": {"workerId": "99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999", "enrolled": false, "enrolledAt": null, "livenessConfidence": null, "photoUrl": null}, "error": null}

response.name: 400 - workerId is not a valid UUID
response.body: {"success": false, "data": null, "error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Invalid value for parameter 'workerId'", "fieldErrors": null, "timestamp": "2026-11-13T06:40:00Z", "traceId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"}}

request.description:
**Permission:** `faceauth.enroll`.

Multipart form-data with two parts: `file` (the reference photo) and `consentGiven`. The caller's IP is recorded server-side as the consent IP (from `X-Forwarded-For`'s last trusted hop, else the socket address) - there is no request field for it.

Re-enrolling a worker who already has a template fully **overwrites** it; there is no history of past enrollments, only ever the current one. The previous enrollment photo is deleted once the new one is stored.

**Validation**, checked in this order (all -> 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, nothing persisted):
1. `consentGiven` must be `true` - enrollment can never proceed without this worker's explicit, recorded consent.
2. `file` must be non-empty and at most 2MB.
3. Its declared `Content-Type` must be exactly `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, or `image/webp`.
4. Its actual leading bytes must match that declared type (magic-byte check - the same guard used on the Masterdata icon uploads).

**Business rules**, checked by the face-auth provider itself once validation passes (all -> 422 `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION`, nothing persisted - ATW never stores a template the provider itself considers unreliable):
1. Image quality must be acceptable - rejection reasons (e.g. too blurry, face too small, poor lighting) come verbatim from the provider.
2. The liveness check must pass - rejects an obvious photo-of-a-photo/spoof attempt.

Locally and in tests, `atw.face-auth.provider` is unset and defaults to a stub adapter that accepts any photo as acceptable-quality and live - the two 422 examples below can only actually be exercised against a real `atw.face-auth.provider=python` deployment of the separate face-auth service (see this collection's folder description).

response.name: 200 - Enrolled (or re-enrolled, overwriting the previous template)
400 - Consent not given
response.body: {"success": false, "data": null, "error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Worker consent is required before enrolling a face template.", "fieldErrors": null, "timestamp": "2026-11-13T06:40:00Z", "traceId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"}}

response.name: 400 - Unsupported file content type
response.body: {"success": false, "data": null, "error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Unsupported image content type: application/pdf (allowed: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp)", "fieldErrors": null, "timestamp": "2026-11-13T06:40:00Z", "traceId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"}}

response.name: 422 - Image quality insufficient
response.body: {"success": false, "data": null, "error": {"code": "BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION", "message": "Image quality is insufficient for enrollment: face too small, image too blurry", "fieldErrors": null, "timestamp": "2026-11-13T06:40:00Z", "traceId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"}}

response.name: 422 - Liveness check failed
response.body: {"success": false, "data": null, "error": {"code": "BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION", "message": "Liveness check failed - please retake the photo of the worker in person.", "fieldErrors": null, "timestamp": "2026-11-13T06:40:00Z", "traceId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"}}

request.description:
**Permission:** `faceauth.enroll` - the same permission as enroll/re-enroll; there is no separate `faceauth.delete`.

Deletes the stored template and its reference photo. **Not an error if nothing was enrolled** - this is a "make sure nothing is enrolled" operation, not a "delete this specific enrollment" one (same convention as Masterdata's Remove Industry Image).

response.name: 400 - workerId is not a valid UUID
response.body: {"success": false, "data": null, "error": {"code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Invalid value for parameter 'workerId'", "fieldErrors": null, "timestamp": "2026-11-13T06:40:00Z", "traceId": "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"}}
